description: Reopened after an external suggestion to rewrite defk in Zig, Rust, V, Odin or Roc. Resolved: no. The verdict measures performance (already at clang parity - all candidates funnel to the same LLVM optimizer; V compiles via C), BEAM protection (design + threat list + sanitizers, language-neutral; Rust safety stops at unsafe FFI and a NIF is 100% FFI), devex (lives in Elixir on Elixir AST, cannot move), agreement (Elixir mode + differential tests, language-neutral). A rewrite re-proves every measurement, tick-gap number, upgrade test and sanitizer run for zero new verdict evidence. Node-crash isolation comes from prevention-by-construction and evidence (defk-gtv closed, defk-5fc, defk-63k, defk-j5n) plus the fault-containment spike (defk-7dm), not from the implementation language.

comments.text: Resolution: no rewrite. Considered 2026-10-08 after an external suggestion (Zig/Rust/V/Odin/Roc). Prevention-by-construction plus evidence (defk-gtv, defk-5fc, defk-63k, defk-j5n) and the fault-containment spike defk-7dm protect the BEAM; the implementation language does not. All candidates funnel to the same LLVM optimizer (or via C), so no codegen-quality gain is possible against the current clang parity. The frontend cannot move (it must run at mix compile over Elixir AST). A rewrite costs weeks of re-proving every measurement, tick-gap number, upgrade test and sanitizer run for zero new verdict evidence.

title: Should defk move to another implementation stack (Zig/Rust/V/Odin/Roc)?
